sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
The petitioners are sought to be prosecuted for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

2. The case of the prosecution is that, accused No.1/husband and accused Nos.2 and 3/parents-in-law NC: 2023:KHC:33885 subjected the defacto complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically and also demand was made to bring money from the parental home.
3. The parties are present before this Court.

The petitioners have annexed a copy of memorandum of settlement under Section 89 of CPC read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005, by which the marriage between the parties has been dissolved mutually and as per the terms of the settlement, accused No.1 has paid a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- towards balance permanent alimony through demand draft and the same is acknowledged by the defacto complainant who is present before this Court, subject to realization.
The second respondent/defacto complainant has no objection to quash the impugned proceedings.

4. Though the offences are cognizable and non compoundable, however having regard to the fact that the parties have amicably resolved the dispute among themselves, and the second Nithin K.C vs State Of Karnataka on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138714663/
2 respondent/defacto complainant having no objection for quashing the impugned proceedings, it would be a futile exercise, if the petitioners are subjected to trial, since the probability of their conviction is remote and bleak in view of the settlement.
